y-m-07-05.title: 1/2 and 1/4 of ribbon: who use more?
y-m-07-05.topic: Fractions only compare when whole same (fractions of different wholes)
y-m-07-05.goal: Understand fraction sizes alone no compare different wholes; identify info needed and make numeric cases where used lengths equal.
y-m-07-05.material: Jian use half of red ribbon; Doyun quarter of blue. Don't know if ribbons initially same length. Each ribbon one whole strip. 1/2 and 1/4 mean equal parts of each person's own ribbon. Read 1/2 "one half," 1/4 "one quarter." 1 1 2 4
y-m-07-05.prereq.0: Fraction tells count of equal parts of a whole
y-m-07-05.s.s1.prompt: Using only what known, who used longer ribbon?
y-m-07-05.s.s1.hint.0: Choose any starting red/blue lengths (e.g. 20cm,40cm) and write each used length.
y-m-07-05.s.s1.hint.1: Change ribbon lengths and see if who uses more changes.
y-m-07-05.s.s1.o.a: We don't know initial lengths, so can't decide.
y-m-07-05.s.s1.r.a: This points out fraction is about its own whole. What info would let you decide?
y-m-07-05.s.s1.r.b: 1/2>1/4 only comparing same whole. Check whether ribbon wholes same first.
y-m-07-05.s.s1.r.c: Bigger denominator no mean longer piece. Different wholes change cm length.
y-m-07-05.s.s1.o.d: Probably Jian. Different wholes are rare
y-m-07-05.s.s1.r.d: No basis for "rare." Try numbers with different wholes.
y-m-07-05.s.s1.explain: 1/2 is greater than 1/4 for same-size ribbons. Example red 20cm: half=10cm. If blue 80cm, quarter=20cm longer; if blue 8cm, quarter=2cm shorter. Need ribbon lengths to decide. 1 1 1 2 4 4

y-m-07-05.s.s2.hint.0: Assume info true, set red ribbon to 20cm; try blue lengths and find used lengths.

y-m-07-05.s.s2.r.b: If wholes same, compare fractions straight away.
y-m-07-05.s.s2.o.c: Both use half or less of own ribbon
y-m-07-05.s.s2.r.c: 1/2,1/4 already half or less; no new info. 1 2
y-m-07-05.s.s2.r.d: If blue shorter, its quarter even shorter; compare with red half. Uses whole-size relation. 1 1 2 4
y-m-07-05.s.s2.r.e: This gives exact whole ratio. You can express 1/4 blue in red units.
y-m-07-05.s.s2.explain: Call red R and blue B. Jian uses R/2, Doyun B/4. If same lengths, Jian more. If blue shorter, Jian still more. If blue 4 times longer, Doyun uses length of R, more than Jian. Just knowing blue longer doesn't show if >2×, so can't decide. 1

y-m-07-02.title: 6 bags with 47 marbles each: three calculation methods
y-m-07-02.topic: Different ways to calculate 2-digit×1-digit by splitting number
y-m-07-02.goal: Find/fix wrong line in split calculations; use examples to check different splits same total and explain why.
y-m-07-02.material: Each bag has 47 marbles, 6 bags total. Three friends make 47 easier then find total. Read 47×6 as "forty-seven times six."
y-m-07-02.thinking.0: Compare three solutions and locate mistake
y-m-07-02.thinking.2: Explain why different methods give same answer

y-m-07-02.s.s1.hint.0: First compare how each friend rewrite 47 line by line.
y-m-07-02.s.s1.hint.1: Compare numbers with 47 and check each addition/subtraction.
y-m-07-02.s.s1.explain: Line 4 wrong. Doha treat 47 as "3 less than 50," so from 50×6=300 must subtract 3×6=18: 300−18=282. Adding make it like calculate 53 instead of 47. Jian and Seoa both get 282.
y-m-07-02.s.s2.prompt: Calculate 47×6 by splitting 47 into a,b. Make 3 easy splits. a,b natural, a+b=47, and one must be multiple of 5. 40+7 and 7+40 count same. 5
y-m-07-02.s.s2.hint.1: Choose multiple of 5, subtract from 47 for other part.
y-m-07-02.s.s2.ok.c3: One of a,b from 5 times table.
y-m-07-02.s.s2.fail.c3: At least one a,b multiple of 5 (5,10,15,...) 10 5
y-m-07-02.s.s2.explain: Examples: 40+7,45+2,35+12,30+17 all total 47 and one multiple 5. Any split, adding (part×6) gives 47×6=282. 12 2 30 35 45 7

y-m-07-02.s.s2.because.hint.0: Write each split result together and compare.
y-m-07-02.s.s2.because.hint.1: Think whether total changes depending on order you count 6 bags of 47.
y-m-07-02.s.s2.because.placeholder: For example: There are ... marbles. Even if split different, ... because ...
y-m-07-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You explain in your own words splitting/calculating/rejoining 47 no change total?
y-m-07-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.2: You connect a+b=47 with why result same?
y-m-07-02.s.s2.because.model.0: There are 282 marbles. However you split 47, you rejoin parts of 6 bags of 47; total remain same.
y-m-07-02.s.s2.because.model.1: Got 282. Whether 40×6+7×6 or 45×6+2×6, total marbles same, so answer same.
y-m-07-02.s.s2.because.modelNote.1: You explain by giving two different splits yourself.
y-m-07-02.s.s2.because.model.2: Even with different splits, 47×6 has one fixed value, so all give 282.

y-m-07-04.title: After 285 of 603 books borrowed, strange subtraction result
y-m-07-04.topic: When vertical subtraction of 3-digit numbers subtract digit-by-digit works and fails
y-m-07-04.goal: Find wrong line in vertical subtraction; choose checks that show result strange; find cases where wrong method happens to work.
y-m-07-04.material: Library had 603 books; 285 borrowed. Eunu do vertical subtraction, say 482 left. 603−285 read "six hundred three minus two hundred eighty-five." Next part give steps.
y-m-07-04.thinking.2: Find conditions under which wrong method works
y-m-07-04.s.s1.prompt: Eunu steps below. Choose one wrong line.
y-m-07-04.s.s1.hint.0: Follow his vertical work by line, starting ones.
y-m-07-04.s.s1.hint.1: When top digit smaller than bottom, what Eunu did; is it same as subtracting 285 from 603?
y-m-07-04.s.s1.line.0: Write 603−285 vertically, calculate from ones place.
y-m-07-04.s.s1.explain: Lines 2 and 3 wrong. When top digit less than bottom, Eunu swapped and subtracted. Instead borrow 10 from next place. Then 603−285=318.
y-m-07-04.s.s2.prompt: Choose all ways to show Eunu answer 482 strange.
y-m-07-04.s.s2.hint.0: For each check, think "does error still appear if I make same mistake as Eunu?"
y-m-07-04.s.s2.hint.1: Apply each check to 482 and state if error appear.
y-m-07-04.s.s2.o.a: Recalculate from start same way as Eunu
y-m-07-04.s.s2.r.a: Same method repeats same mistake and same result. Need different method.
y-m-07-04.s.s2.r.b: This checks subtraction by reversing with addition, different path, so catch error.
y-m-07-04.s.s2.o.c: Check if 482 fewer than starting 603 books
y-m-07-04.s.s2.r.c: 482 below 603. Wrong answer also passes, so alone no reveal.
y-m-07-04.s.s2.o.d: Estimate 603 and 285 to see approximate books left
y-m-07-04.s.s2.r.d: Estimate and compare with 482. Can spot answer far off without detailed work.
y-m-07-04.s.s2.explain: 482+285=767, not 603, wrong. 603 about 600, 285 about 300, so about 300 remain; 482 much more. Repeating same method or only checking 482<603 no reveal.
y-m-07-04.s.s2.acc.0: Adding is exact check. See if estimate can check too.
y-m-07-04.s.s2.acc.1: Estimate show result far off. Is there exact check with addition too?
y-m-07-04.s.s3.prompt: Some subtractions where Eunu method (larger digit minus smaller digit in each place) happens to be correct. Make 2 different examples where his result equals correct. y-m-07-03.title: Same calculation, different answers depending on story
y-m-07-03.topic: Cases where quotient/remainder used differently in stories
y-m-07-03.goal: Interpret division quotient/remainder to fit story question and make own stories where same calculation answers differ.
y-m-07-03.material: Autumn field trip: 50 students ride boats. Boats identical, max 8 people each. No student left behind. 50÷8 gives quotient 6 remainder 2. Check: 8×6+2=50.

y-m-07-03.s.s1.hint.1: Find how many left after full boats; where they ride?
y-m-07-03.s.s1.r.a: This read quotient 6 as boat count. Check if anyone unable to ride in 6 full boats.
y-m-07-03.s.s1.r.b: This read capacity 8 as boat count. 8 na people one boat carry.
y-m-07-03.s.s1.r.c: This read remainder 2 as boat count. 2 na leftover people.
y-m-07-03.s.s1.r.d: This included fact leftover students need place too.
y-m-07-03.s.s1.explain: 6 boats carry 48, 2 remain. Those 2 also need ride, so one more boat: 7 total. Answer not quotient 6, but one more.
y-m-07-03.s.s2.prompt: If student number change, boat count change. Make 3 situations needing exactly 10 boats with last boat not full. Students n, capacity c. Capacity natural 2 to 9; all ride.

y-m-07-03.s.s2.fail.c4: Boat count no be 10. Divide students by capacity; check full boats and leftovers.
y-m-07-03.s.s2.explain: Example 75 students, capacity 8: 75÷8 quotient 9 remainder 3. Three left after 9 full boats need another, so 10 boats. Same capacity can keep quotient same while remainder changes by student count. 3

y-m-07-03.s.s3.hint.0: Think other container or purchase stories, like buy with 50원.
